First, I'll parse the SVG path data. The path has multiple line commands (L) connecting points:

- Start at (29.40, 69.39)
- Line to (51.16, 67.08)
- Line to (65.98, 58.97)
- Line to (86.05, 37.54)
- Line to (83.22, 21.48)
- Then "M" (move) to (83.22, 21.48) — this is the same point, so it continues from there
- Line to (41.67, 26.57)
- Line to (29.40, 69.39) — back to start

So the points in order are:
1. (29.40, 69.39)
2. (51.16, 67.08)
3. (65.98, 58.97)
4. (86.05, 37.54)
5. (83.22, 21.48)
6. (41.67, 26.57)
7. Back to (29.40, 69.39)

That's 6 distinct vertices connected in sequence, forming a closed shape. A closed shape with 6 vertices is a hexagon.

Checking geometric principles:
- All segments are straight lines (L commands)
- The path closes back to the start point
- 6 vertices → hexagon
- Not a triangle (3 sides), pentagon (5), heptagon (7), or octagon (8)
- Not a circle (no curves), not a sector (no radial edges), not a kite (4 sides), not a rectangle (4 sides with right angles), not a single line

Final answer: (C)
